papers.title: Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.

papers.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, II. Operator-Theoretic Tools
papers.abstract: This is the second part of a two-part work on semiclassical Weyl laws and Connes' integration formulas for spectral triples. It establishes three operator-theoretic results, which are used in Part I but are of independent interest. The first is a factorization formula for the fractional commutators $[|D|^{-\alpha},a]$, which is obtained by means of double operator integrals. The second is an enhancement, for arbitrary unital spectral triples, of a lemma of Connes-Sukochev-Zanin on the differences $(a^{1/2}|D|^{-\alpha}a^{1/2})^s-|D|^{-\alpha s}a^s$, together with a holomorphic version of it. The third is a Tauberian theorem showing that zeta function and heat trace conditions of the type sought by Connes imply Weyl laws for the operators $aD^2a$, where $a$ ranges over positive invertible elements of the algebra. Along the way, we obtain a version for spectral triples of the Tauberian theorem of McDonald-Sukochev-Zanin without any extra regularity assumption or restriction on the degree of summability. This paper can be read largely independently of Part I.

papers.title: Freeness conditions for intermediate $C^*$-algebras of crossed products
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a separable $C^*$-algebra, let $\Gamma$ be a discrete countable group, let $\alpha: \Gamma \to \text{Aut}(B)$ be an action, and let $A$ be an invariant subalgebra. We find certain freeness conditions which guarantee that any intermediate $C^*$-algebra $A \rtimes_{\alpha,r} \Gamma \subseteq C \subseteq B \rtimes_{\alpha,r} \Gamma$ is a crossed product of an intermediate invariant subalgebra $A \subseteq C_0 \subseteq B$ by $\Gamma$. Those are used to generalize related results by Suzuki.

papers.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, I. Main Results
papers.abstract: In this paper, we combine techniques from functional analysis and spectral theory to obtain semiclassical Weyl laws and extensions of Connes' integration formula for a large class of spectral triples. These results generalize and simplify recent work of McDonald--Sukochev--Zanin: all regularity assumptions and dimension restrictions are removed, and their Tauberian condition is replaced by a weaker spectral condition, Condition~(W), which holds in far greater generality. We also establish Tauberian criteria for Condition~(W) involving zeta functions and heat traces, as sought by Alain Connes. The results are illustrated on bounded Euclidean domains, closed Riemannian manifolds, the Steklov problem, and quantum tori. In the latter setting they resolve a conjecture of Edward McDonald and the author. This is the first part of a two-part work. The proofs of the main technical results are given in Part II.

papers.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
papers.abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers. Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Di\c{t}\u{a}'s family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.

papers.title: A major origin of quantumness
papers.abstract: A system property is considered to be elementary, when any further refined specification is impossible. Any two elementary properties of a classical system mutually exclude each other. However, this does not hold anymore for a quantum system, where mutual exclusivity becomes a special relation. This orthogonality relation becomes our first axiom. It is sufficient to define states in an abstract setting and we then introduce two simple, but far-reaching further basic axioms for the states, which mimic the quantum mechanical correspondence between the pure states and the rank-one projections. All examples that we can identify origin from operator algebras or certain Jordan algebras and require the Gleason theorem. The identification of further cases is an unresolved challenge. If some exist, they might result in promising new mathematical models for an extended quantum theory. The non-existence would mean that our extremely basic postulates bring us unexpectedly close to common quantum theory. In any case, the distinction between inequality and mutual exclusivity of elementary system properties appears to be a major origin of quantumness. Our basic approach does not encompass the non-atomic von Neumann algebras of type II and III, which play a crucial role in quantum field theory, and we present a modification of the axioms to include them.

papers.title: Invariance of Property (T) for \'Etale Groupoids
papers.abstract: We study topological Property (T) for locally compact Hausdorff \'etale groupoids under pullbacks, amplifications, and Morita equivalencen. We show that Kazhdan pairs for the regular representation family pull back along Haar system-preserving homomorphisms, and for general representation families we identify a constant-vector compatibility condition as the additional hypothesis needed. We also show that Property (T) for the regular representation family passes from a groupoid to its transformation groupoid with the same Kazhdan constant; under a natural restriction condition on representation families, the same holds for general families. Finally, we prove that Property (T) is invariant under ampliation for ample groupoids with compact unit spaces, both for all representations and for the regular representation family. Hence topological Property (T) is Morita invariant for ample Hausdorff \'etale groupoids with compact unit spaces, and likewise for the regular representation family.

papers.title: A new second-moment method for spectral measures of inhomogeneous non-Hermitian random matrices
papers.abstract: We develop a second-moment method for the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of non-Hermitian random matrices $X_N=(\sqrt{s_{ij}}\xi_{ij})$ with a deterministic variance profile $S_N=(s_{ij})$. When the entries are independent and centered, the second moment of $\det(zI-X_N)$ is the permanent $\mathrm{per}(S_N+|z|^2I)$ of a diagonal shift of $S_N$, and the method approximates $\log|\det(zI-X_N)|$ by half its logarithm. For i.i.d. centered $\xi_{ij}$ of unit variance satisfying a Dini-type condition on their L\'evy concentration function, we prove the circular law for every doubly stochastic profile whose largest entry tends to zero, however slowly. This condition holds for every law with a bounded density on $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We also allow the two entries $X_{ij}$ and $X_{ji}$ of each reciprocal pair to be correlated, with a nondegenerate joint law that has a finite mixed fourth moment. If the pairs and the diagonal entries also have bounded densities on their real linear supports, we prove an elliptic law for every symmetric doubly stochastic profile whose largest entry tends to zero. For i.i.d. $\xi_{ij}$ as above and general profiles with vanishing largest entry and bounded average row sum, we show that the ESD is asymptotically close to the Brown measure of the matrix $(\sqrt{s_{ij}}c_{ij})$ of free circular elements. The ESD converges weakly in probability if and only if $N^{-1}\log\mathrm{per}(S_N+qI)$ converges for every $q>0$, and these limits determine the radial distribution of the limit. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for convergence in terms of tree weights, characterize the radial laws that arise from profiles with uniformly bounded row and column sums, and show that the empirical distribution of the zeros of $\mathrm{per}(zI-X_N)$ is asymptotically close to the ESD.

papers.title: Subfactor symmetries of real Hadamard matrices
papers.abstract: Every Hadamard matrix gives rise to a {\it spin model commuting square} and a hyperfinite subfactor with finite Jones index. The standard invariant of this subfactor is comprised of quantum symmetries of the subfactor which can be viewed as ``non-invertible'' symmetries of the Hadamard matrix. We show that if the Hadamard matrix is real and has order greater than four and congruent to four modulo eight, the standard invariant is minimal, i.e. it consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Consequently, both principal graphs of the subfactor are $A_\infty$. In particular, this holds for every Paley type II Hadamard matrix. The proof uses a congruence for products of four rows and Jones's annular decomposition. More generally, we show that if an irreducible subfactor of finite index greater than four has bounded annular multiplicities along an infinite subsequence of degrees, then its principal graph is $A_\infty$.

papers.title: Equivalences of C*-correspondence relations
papers.abstract: We study three relations between C*-correspondences that lie between strong shift equivalence and shift equivalence, called aligned, balanced, and compatible shift equivalence. We show that for regular and full C*-correspondences, the three relations coincide.

papers.title: Complemented Copies of $c_{0}$ in Positive Tensor Products of Banach Lattices
papers.abstract: A result of Cembranos states that a non-trivial injective tensor product of a $C$-space contains a complemented copy of $c_{0}$, and in particular fails the Grothendieck property. We establish a positive analogue of the Cembranos theorem for tensor products of Banach lattices. If $E$ and $F$ are infinite dimensional Banach lattices, one of which contains a copy of $c_{0}$, then the Wittstock tensor product $E\widetilde{\otimes}_{\vert{\varepsilon}\vert}F$ contains a complemented copy of $c_{0}$. If $F$ is in addition reflexive, then $E\widetilde{\otimes}_{\vert{\varepsilon}\vert}F$ fails the positive Grothendieck property.

papers.title: Minkowskian open/closed conformal field theory possibly without vacuum: the Cardy case
papers.abstract: For any conformal net, not necessarily rational, we construct the associated Cardy-type conformal field theory on the Minkowski spacetimes $(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R$ for closed strings and $[0,\pi]\times\mathbb R$ for open strings within the framework of algebraic quantum field theory. In addition to verifying some of their basic properties, we prove three forms of Haag duality for multi-double-cones and boundary intervals, interpreted respectively as the Minkowskian versions of modular invariance, the Cardy consistency condition, and the Morita equivalence of boundary field algebras.
